reviewerDerivedProposition: Acute dyspnoea arising 45 minutes into a second unit, accompanied by hypertension, new jugular venous distension, a new S3 gallop, crackles extending well beyond the chronic bibasilar baseline, worsening peripheral oedema and falling urine output, in a client with chronic kidney disease and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, is transfusion-associated circulatory overload. The differentiating cue is the volume-overload cluster itself: transfusion-related acute lung injury is defined by the ABSENCE of circulatory overload, anaphylaxis would bring urticaria, wheeze, angio-oedema and hypotension rather than hypertension, and a febrile non-haemolytic reaction would not produce this respiratory and haemodynamic picture.
requiredFacts: The Stage 2 reaction findings in full - stage_2.

The chronic baseline against which they are new - faint chronic bibasilar crackles, no JVD at 45 degrees, trace ankle oedema, BP 138/82, SpO2 96 percent - baseline_assessment_labs. Without this the learner cannot tell which Stage 2 findings are new.
The cardiac and renal risk history - baseline_history_protocol.
Explicit absence of allergic features at Stage 2 - no urticaria, hives, angio-oedema, wheeze, itching or throat tightness - which is what defeats the anaphylaxis option.
Nothing in stage_3 or stage_4 is required.
disclosureEvidence: Stage hiding is necessary and would be sufficient if stages were the only surface: stage_3 reports a chest film 'consistent with hydrostatic pulmonary edema' with the explicit note that the patchy infiltrates characteristic of non-cardiogenic oedema are absent, plus a BNP rise from 280 to 890, and stage_4 records the provider's documented diagnosis of transfusion-associated circulatory overload outright. BUT THE DECISIVE DISCLOSURE IS NOT IN A STAGE. Sibling q4's stem reads 'Which actions belong in the management plan for this suspected TACO episode?' and sibling q6's stem reads 'Which Stage 3 and Stage 4 findings best show that the TACO episode is resolving?'. Both siblings are baseline-anchored, so they render, and a stem is always rendered regardless of anchor. Under P23 a case study is one top-level question with one aggregate submit and true unfolding reveal is deferred, so all parts are on screen together. A learner answering q2's reaction dropdown can read the answer off two sibling stems. Separately and more weakly, the parent title 'Transfusion-associated circulatory overload versus transfusion-related acute lung injury' frames the differential and collapses a four-option dropdown to a two-way choice, with the correct answer named first.
clinicalVerdict: Both keys are clinically correct and the item is well built. Verified that hypertension is characteristically seen in TACO whereas hypotension is more common in TRALI; that elevated jugular venous pressure, an S3 on auscultation and an elevated BNP suggest TACO; and that TRALI diagnosis specifically requires that there be no evidence of circulatory overload such as an S3 gallop or jugular distension. The keyed evidence cluster is therefore exactly the discriminating set, and the case supports each element at Stage 2 against an explicit baseline. The anaphylaxis and febrile-reaction distractors are properly defeated by findings the case documents as absent rather than by omission. The evidence options are also well constructed, since the TRALI option is phrased as hypoxaemia with bilateral infiltrates but no circulatory overload, which is the correct definitional contrast. I found no clinical error, no invented fact and no key ambiguity. THE DEFECT IS DISCLOSURE THROUGH SIBLING STEMS, NOT CLINICAL.
contentDefects: PRIMARY: sibling stems q4 and q6 name TACO explicitly and render alongside q2, disclosing the keyed answer of the reaction dropdown. Neither stem can be hidden by this row's anchor.

SECONDARY, MEDIUM confidence: the bilingual parent title names both candidate diagnoses as the case's framing, narrowing the four-option dropdown to two and listing the correct answer first. This is weaker than the three title defects found earlier in this review, where the title named the answer outright rather than the differential, and I record it as a lesser concern rather than an independent blocker.

OBSERVATION, out of scope: non-residual sibling q1 is baseline-anchored yet its stem asks the learner to highlight Stage 2 findings, so it cites a stage its own boundary hides. I note it because the integration seat will be touching this parent, but q1 is not a residual row and I make no finding on it.
bilingualVerdict: PARALLEL - stem, clozeStem, all eight dropdown options across the two dropdowns, both keys, rationale, both byChoice entries and strategy are semantically equivalent EN/ZH. The title frames the differential identically in Chinese, and the sibling stems name TACO in both languages, so any repair is bilingual.
sourcesChecked: Transfusion reaction literature located via NIH and AABB domain search, including the AABB association bulletin on TACO and peer-reviewed TACO/TRALI differentiation work - verified that hypertension is characteristic of TACO while hypotension is more common in TRALI, that elevated jugular venous pressure, S3 and elevated BNP favour TACO, and that TRALI requires the absence of circulatory-overload evidence such as S3 or jugular distension. Also noted, though not load-bearing here, that natriuretic peptides have only moderate accuracy for this differentiation - the item does not rely on BNP, which sits in the hidden stage_3.
Direct inspection of all five sibling parts for mentions of the diagnosis, which produced the decisive finding.
siblingImpact: HIGH. The disclosure originates in sibling parts, not in this row. q4 and q6 are non-residual and already accepted, so removing 'TACO' from their stems is a change to accepted content requiring its own review. The title is a global surface visible to all six parts. This row cannot be remediated without touching at least one surface outside itself.
repairConstraints: Recognise that anchoring does not close this row. Set the boundary to stage_2, which is correct and necessary, but do not treat the anchor as the repair.

Choose a route for the sibling disclosure. Either re-scope q2 so it no longer asks the learner to name the reaction and instead assesses the discriminating evidence cluster alone, which is confined to the residual row and is my recommendation; or neutralise the diagnosis wording in the q4 and q6 stems, which reaches accepted content and needs its own independent review.
If the title is also neutralised, prefer a presenting-problem framing such as acute dyspnoea during transfusion in a client with chronic kidney disease, in EN and ZH.
Preserve both dropdown keys and all eight option texts; the clinical content is correct and well sourced.
Anchor to stage_2 after repair. Baseline is not available: the entire reaction exists only in stage_2.
criticalNote: This is the fourth parent in this review where a diagnosis is disclosed outside the residual row's reach, and the third where sibling surfaces rather than the title are the binding constraint. The pattern is now consistent enough that I recommend the integration seat run a whole-parent diagnosis-mention survey on every parent containing a diagnostic-identification item, rather than inspecting titles alone.
agreementReasoning: Codex proposes stage_2 with no content work, and its stage reasoning is right as far as it goes - stage_3's imaging and BNP and stage_4's explicit diagnosis must indeed be hidden. I reach the same boundary independently. But the producer treated stage hiding as sufficient and did not survey the sibling surfaces. I did, and found that two baseline-anchored sibling stems name TACO in plain text and render on the same screen as q2 under P23, which hands the learner the reaction dropdown regardless of any anchor. An absence of proposed content edits is not evidence the boundary closes the row, and here it does not. Disposition changed from ANCHOR_ONLY_REPAIR_CANDIDATE to CONTENT_REPAIR_REQUIRED, boundary retained at stage_2.
